title: Adaptive Quantum Security of LRQ
summary: The existing adaptive LRQ proof fails because required construction-input information is absent from the compressed-oracle database; finding a valid security proof remains open.

formal_statement.body: Establish adaptive quantum security of LRQ without relying on bad predicates that use input information absent from the oracle database.

scope.domain: Adaptive quantum security proofs for the LRQ construction using compressed-oracle techniques.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove adaptive quantum security of LRQ without bad predicates that depend on input information absent from the oracle database.

citations.label: Mind the Bad Norms: Revisiting Compressed Oracle-based Quantum Indistinguishability Proofs

progress.summary: The source explains that the bad-database technique requires information present in the database, while part of the LRQ construction input never appears there. The supplied context treats this as a fundamental obstacle to the existing adaptive proof.
citation_labels: Ritam Bhaumik et al., Mind the Bad Norms: Revisiting Compressed Oracle-based Quantum Indistinguishability Proofs
